sourceQuestions.sourceText: Draw a line to join the words that rhyme. hot cool sun bees / fun spot trees pool
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: hot – spot • cool – pool • sun – fun • bees – trees

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Do the words rhyme, or start the same? Write each pair in the right box. drip – drop, puddles – huddles, splish – splash, play – stay
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Rhyme: puddles – huddles, play – stay • Start the same: drip – drop, splish – splash

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Circle the verbs that end with ing. a We are going to the park. b Mum is bringing a picnic.
Circle the correct verb. a Yesterday, it raining / rained. b Tomorrow, it will be snowing / snowed. c Stop / Stopped shouting!
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a rained • b snowing • c Stop

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Finish the poem with a rhyming word. It is hot in the sun, I'm having some ___. I'll go in the pool, to keep myself ___.
Finish the storm line with an ing verb: The thunder is ___.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any ing verb that suits thunder: booming, crashing, banging, rumbling

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Read: "The thunder crashed. Sara hid under the blanket and held her teddy tight." How does Sara feel?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Scared / frightened — she hid and held her teddy tight.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write your own two-line poem about rain or sun.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Two lines about rain or sun. Extra praise if the last words rhyme.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Which pair rhymes? ( drip – drop ) ( cool – pool ) ( sun – rain )
"Splish, splash" are two words that ( start the same ) ( mean the same ) ( are names )
A good listener ( talks at the same time ) ( looks away ) ( looks at the person talking )
Yesterday, we ___ in the puddles. ( jumping ) ( jumped ) ( jump )
In "Mum is bringing a picnic", the ing verb is ( bringing ) ( picnic ) ( Mum )
